item.title: Sierpinski carpet in micro(A) 14F
item.dc:creator: aurel
item.description:
with RECT x,y,w,h

Code:
' Micro(A) - Sierpinski Tepih pomocu RECT naredbe
mode 1 : wcolor 0,0,0: swap

fcolor 100, 150, 255 ' Plava boja za kvadrate

' Pokrecemo crtanje (X, Y, velicina, dubina)
drawCarpet(150, 50, 500, 4)

swap

func drawCarpet(var x, var y, var size, var depth)
    ' LOKALNE VARIJABLE: Sve na samom vrhu zbog stoga!
    var subSize
    var x1, x2, x3
    var y1, y2, y3

    if depth = 0
        ' BAZNI SLUCAJ: Samo jedna brza naredba umjesto 4 linije!
        rect x, y, size, size
       ' return
    else
        ' Izracunaj velicinu manjih kvadrata
        subSize = size / 3

        ' Definišemo tri X i Y pozicije u mreži
        x1 = x
        x2 = x + subSize
        x3 = x + subSize * 2

        y1 = y
        y2 = y + subSize
        y3 = y + subSize * 2

        ' REKURZIVNI POZIVI: 8 okolnih kvadrata
        ' Gornji red
        drawCarpet(x1, y1, subSize, depth - 1)
        drawCarpet(x2, y1, subSize, depth - 1)
        drawCarpet(x3, y1, subSize, depth - 1)

        ' Srednji red (bez sredine!)
        drawCarpet(x1, y2, subSize, depth - 1)
        drawCarpet(x3, y2, subSize, depth - 1)

        ' Donji red
        drawCarpet(x1, y3, subSize, depth - 1)
        drawCarpet(x2, y3, subSize, depth - 1)
        drawCarpet(x3, y3, subSize, depth - 1)
    endif
endfn

item.title: Mini Debugger
item.dc:creator: Nelson
item.description:
Built a small but maybe useful debugger for NaaLaa 7 if anyone is interested. 

Code:
visible dbgEnabled = true
visible dbgOverlay = true
visible dbgPaused = false
visible dbgStepOnce = false
visible dbgProject = "App"

visible dbgBreaks = []        ' table: tag -> true
visible dbgWatches = []       ' array of [name, valueText]
visible dbgLogs = []          ' ring buffer
visible dbgLogMax = 200
visible dbgLastBreak = ""
visible dbgFrame = 0

function dbgInit(projectName)
    dbgProject = projectName
    dbgEnabled = true
    dbgOverlay = true
    dbgPaused = false
    dbgStepOnce = false
    dbgBreaks = []
    dbgWatches = []
    dbgLogs = []
    dbgLastBreak = ""
    dbgFrame = 0
    dbgLog("Debugger initialized: " + projectName)
endfunc

function dbgAddBreak(tag)
    dbgBreaks[tag] = true
    dbgLog("Breakpoint added: " + tag)
endfunc

function dbgRemoveBreak(tag)
    if key(dbgBreaks, tag) <> 0
        free key dbgBreaks, tag
        dbgLog("Breakpoint removed: " + tag)
    endif
endfunc

function dbgBreak(tag)
    if not dbgEnabled then return
    if key(dbgBreaks, tag) <> 0
        dbgPaused = true
        dbgLastBreak = tag
        dbgLog("BREAK: " + tag)
    endif
endfunc

function dbgPause()
    if not dbgEnabled then return
    dbgPaused = true
    dbgLog("Paused")
endfunc

function dbgContinue()
    if not dbgEnabled then return
    dbgPaused = false
    dbgStepOnce = false
    dbgLog("Continue")
endfunc

function dbgStep()
    if not dbgEnabled then return
    dbgStepOnce = true
    dbgPaused = false
    dbgLog("Step")
endfunc

function dbgLog(msg)
    if not dbgEnabled then return

    lin = "[" + clock() + "] " + msg
    dbgLogs[sizeof(dbgLogs)] = lin

    while sizeof(dbgLogs) > dbgLogMax
        free key dbgLogs, 0
    wend

    pln "[dbg] " + lin
endfunc

function dbgWatch(name, valueText)
    if not dbgEnabled then return

    i = 0
    while i < sizeof(dbgWatches)
        if dbgWatches[i][0] = name
            dbgWatches[i][1] = valueText
            return
        endif
        i = i + 1
    wend

    dbgWatches[sizeof(dbgWatches)] = [name, valueText]
endfunc

function dbgHandleInput()
    if not dbgEnabled then return

    if keydown(KEY_F1, true)
        dbgOverlay = not dbgOverlay
    endif

    if keydown(KEY_F2, true)
        if dbgPaused
            dbgContinue()
        else
            dbgPause()
        endif
    endif

    if keydown(KEY_F3, true)
        dbgStep()
    endif
endfunc

function dbgCanRunFrame()
    if not dbgEnabled then return true

    if dbgPaused
        return false
    endif

    if dbgStepOnce
        dbgStepOnce = false
        dbgPaused = true
    endif

    dbgFrame = dbgFrame + 1
    return true
endfunc

function dbgDrawOverlay()
    if not dbgEnabled or not dbgOverlay then return

    panelX = 8
    panelY = 8
    panelW = 560
    panelH = 220

    set color 20, 24, 30, 220
    draw rect panelX, panelY, panelW, panelH, true
    set color 120, 160, 220
    draw rect panelX, panelY, panelW, 1, true
    draw rect panelX, panelY + panelH - 1, panelW, 1, true

    set color 230, 230, 230
    set caret panelX + 8, panelY + 8
    write "MiniDbg | " + dbgProject + " | frame=" + dbgFrame

    set color 255, 210, 120
    set caret panelX + 8, panelY + 26
    if dbgPaused
        write "State: PAUSED  (F2 continue, F3 step, F1 hide)"
    else
        write "State: RUNNING (F2 pause, F1 hide)"
    endif

    set color 190, 210, 255
    set caret panelX + 8, panelY + 44
    write "Last break: " + dbgLastBreak

    set color 200, 255, 200
    set caret panelX + 8, panelY + 64
    write "Watches:"
    wy = panelY + 82
    i = 0
    while i < sizeof(dbgWatches) and i < 6
        set caret panelX + 14, wy
        write dbgWatches[i][0] + " = " + dbgWatches[i][1]
        wy = wy + 16
        i = i + 1
    wend

    set color 255, 190, 190
    set caret panelX + 300, panelY + 64
    write "Logs:"
    ly = panelY + 82
    start = sizeof(dbgLogs) - 6
    if start < 0 then start = 0

    i = start
    while i < sizeof(dbgLogs)
        set caret panelX + 306, ly
        write dbgLogs[i]
        ly = ly + 16
        i = i + 1
    wend
endfunc
Sample:
Code:
' debugger_demo.n7
' ----------------
' Sample program for the MiniDbg overlay library (debugger.n7).
'
' A ball bounces around the window. The debugger overlay shows live
' watches (position, velocity, bounce count) and a log of events.
'
' Controls:
'   F1  toggle the debug overlay
'   F2  pause / continue
'   F3  step one frame while paused
'   F4  toggle the "bounce" breakpoint (on by default)
'   F5  write a manual log entry
'
' With the "bounce" breakpoint enabled, the program pauses itself every
' time the ball hits a wall. Press F2 to continue or F3 to step.

include "debugger.n7"

constant WIN_W = 640
constant WIN_H = 360

set window "MiniDbg demo", WIN_W, WIN_H
set redraw off

dbgInit("MiniDbg demo")
dbgAddBreak("bounce")

ballX = WIN_W/2
ballY = WIN_H/2
velX = 3
velY = 2
radius = 10
bounces = 0
bounceBreakOn = true

do
    ' Let the debugger react to F1/F2/F3.
    dbgHandleInput()

    ' F4 toggles the "bounce" breakpoint.
    if keydown(KEY_F4, true)
        bounceBreakOn = not bounceBreakOn
        if bounceBreakOn
            dbgAddBreak("bounce")
        else
            dbgRemoveBreak("bounce")
        endif
    endif

    ' F5 writes a manual log entry.
    if keydown(KEY_F5, true)
        dbgLog("Manual log entry, bounces=" + bounces)
    endif

    ' Only update the game when the debugger allows it (running or
    ' single-stepping). Rendering keeps going so the overlay stays live.
    if dbgCanRunFrame()
        ballX = ballX + velX
        ballY = ballY + velY

        hitWall = false
        if ballX < radius
            ballX = radius
            velX = -velX
            hitWall = true
        endif
        if ballX > WIN_W - radius
            ballX = WIN_W - radius
            velX = -velX
            hitWall = true
        endif
        if ballY < radius
            ballY = radius
            velY = -velY
            hitWall = true
        endif
        if ballY > WIN_H - radius
            ballY = WIN_H - radius
            velY = -velY
            hitWall = true
        endif

        if hitWall
            bounces = bounces + 1
            ' Pauses the program if the "bounce" breakpoint is set.
            dbgBreak("bounce")
        endif

        ' Keep the watch panel up to date.
        dbgWatch("ballX", str(ballX))
        dbgWatch("ballY", str(ballY))
        dbgWatch("velX", str(velX))
        dbgWatch("velY", str(velY))
        dbgWatch("bounces", str(bounces))
    endif

    ' --- render ---
    set color 0, 32, 48
    cls

    set color 255, 160, 0
    draw ellipse ballX, ballY, radius, radius, true

    set color 255, 255, 255
    set caret WIN_W/2, WIN_H - 40
    center "F1 overlay  F2 pause/continue  F3 step"
    center "F4 toggle bounce breakpoint  F5 log entry"

    ' Draw the debugger overlay on top of everything.
    dbgDrawOverlay()

    redraw
    fwait 60
until keydown(KEY_ESCAPE, true)

item.title: Alien Breed 3D HD
item.dc:creator: Marcus
item.description:
A long, long time ago, everyone fought to make a DOOM clone for the Amiga. When it came to gameplay I think that Alien Breed 3D was the best attempt, but it looked horrible with a stamp sized low resolution display. This port was recently released, and you can play it in your browser, awesome, I just played to level 4:

https://retro-foundry.github.io/abhd/

item.title: Are you using AI?
item.dc:creator: aliensoldier
item.description:
I’d like to hear your thoughts on whether you’re using AI and what you think of it.

I’ve used it myself, and it makes a lot of mistakes—it mixes up programming languages, and you have to keep a very close eye on it to get anything close to what you actually want. If you’ve been using it for an hour or so, it starts to get confused, and long responses often get cut off halfway through.

In my view, it’s still far too immature for any serious use. Yet, lately, I’ve noticed a lot of games being released for retro systems that rely on AI—in the development of emulators and game engines, and even for translations—and the results are consistently quite mediocre.

If you’ve been using it for an hour or so, it starts to get confused, and long responses often get cut off halfway through.

In my view, it’s still far too immature for any serious use. Yet, lately, I’ve noticed a lot of games being released for retro systems that rely on AI—in the development of emulators and game engines, and even for translations—and the results are consistently quite mediocre.

item.title: Back to racing
item.dc:creator: Marcus
item.description:
Some years ago, before I created the s3d library, we were doing some retro racing game experiments here. The other day I got some ideas for track generation and decided to return to this type of games.



Here I'm creating a smooth and looped track from a simple/rough polygon in a rather complicated way. The curves of the track are then converted into x offsets that can be used for the fake 3d effect.

Edit: Yes, I let gemini generate the assets.

item.title: Monday Morning Marine (w.i.p)
item.dc:creator: Marcus
item.description:
Attached is a playable version of that DOOM style game from the Sokoban thread.



"It's Monday morning, you're totally out of coffee and your (admittedly quite odd) workplace has been infested by demons, robots and slimey creatures
... Ye, it's just another first person shooter."

Move with WASD, shoot with the left mouse button and open doors with spacebar. You can lose stamina but not yet die. Just find the exit to end the game.

I'm not sure if my versions of n7 and enginea are the same as the public ones, so I've included an exe file for the game. But if the mouse sensitivity feels wrong you can try to change line 274:

Code:
vPlayer.SetMouseSens(0.75)

, set a different value, and compile the program - hopefully it works.

I plan to make some real levels. This is just a testing area.

Edit: Do NOT look at the code, cover your eyes if you need to compile it! It's a complete mess without structure! I just took one of the enginea examples and started adding code all over the place. I'll fix it. Structure it. Make it good(lier).
